body:
Could you provide an example of the python script that causes the problem?

The problem seems to come from the reflection of computed columns that was added in 1.3.16

I think that the problem is on this line:
the `.` is not casted like the other fields
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/06ba82a9c74885d1c5d8da7d138a869d83167cae/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py#L2581

```
from sqlalchemy import *
...
  self.engine = create_engine(config.sql_engine_url(), echo=False, pool_pre_ping=True)
  self.connection = self.engine.connect()
  self.metadata = MetaData(schema='_Core')
  for t in ('MemberRegistration', 'UpdateLog'):
    self.cores[t.lower()] = Table(
        t, self.metadata, autoload_with=self.connection)
    # ^^^ error
...
```

The problems seems caused by the used mssql version. The pipeline only test version 2016 I think.

Could you try if this patch works in your system?
```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
index 43f3aeb04..b8a4f8243 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
@@ -2673,7 +2673,9 @@ class MSDialect(default.DefaultDialect):
             )
             table_fullname = "%s.%s" % (owner, tablename)
             concat = func.concat(
-                columns.c.table_schema, ".", columns.c.table_name
+                columns.c.table_schema,
+                sql.literal(".", ischema.CoerceUnicode),
+                columns.c.table_name,
             )
             join_on = computed_cols.c.object_id == func.object_id(concat)
         else:
```
I've changed `sql.cast` to `sql.literal` since cast produces two casts (that works, but this way only one is produced)
well, it is on line # 2581 in my copy of code base. I changed as you suggested, no difference: still the same error.

Sorry, I was on master when I copied that diff.

On which version of mssql are you using and which version of the dbpai are you using?
You mentioned that on mac you do not have this problem. Which version of dbapi are you using there?

MS SQL Server 2017.
TDS 4.2 on Linux, TDS 7.4 on macOS. Ops are somehow unwilling to upgrade TDS on these systems :-(

I've managed to test using tds version 4.2 and the problem was in the returned definition column.

This time this diff should fix it
```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
index 6e2b2f94c..e0e4af763 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/base.py
@@ -2592,12 +2592,10 @@ class MSDialect(default.DefaultDialect):
             join_on, columns.c.column_name == computed_cols.c.name
         )
         join = columns.join(computed_cols, onclause=join_on, isouter=True)
+        # Cast is required by tds_version 4.2
+        computed_definition = sql.cast(computed_cols.c.definition, TEXT)
         s = sql.select(
-            [
-                columns,
-                computed_cols.c.definition,
-                computed_cols.c.is_persisted,
-            ],
+            [columns, computed_definition, computed_cols.c.is_persisted],
             whereclause,
             from_obj=join,
             order_by=[columns.c.ordinal_position],
@@ -2618,7 +2616,7 @@ class MSDialect(default.DefaultDialect):
             numericscale = row[columns.c.numeric_scale]
             default = row[columns.c.column_default]
             collation = row[columns.c.collation_name]
-            definition = row[computed_cols.c.definition]
+            definition = row[computed_definition]
             is_persisted = row[computed_cols.c.is_persisted]

             coltype = self.ischema_names.get(type_, None)
```
yep, this latest patch fixes it

Great, I'll propose a patch tomorrow, so that next version should be fixes.

Thanks for bearing with me and testing the patches 👍

I wonder why this one column has this issue ?  there is a CoerceUnicode datatype in information_schema but it currently doesn't CAST for the actual selected column as that hasn't been a problem.   is there something unique about this column?

It's the only text one that comes from the `sys` schema. They all should be of type nvarchar, but maybe the information schema does not return unicode?

You can force the old tds version by adding `?tds_version=4.2` at the end of a pymssql connection string

> The pipeline only test version 2016 I think.

Currently just 2017.
This problems seems to be connected with the tds version, since I was able to reproduce on version 2019. It affects only tds 4.2. Version 7+ do not have it
TDS version 4.2 is *ancient*. IIRC it pre-dates SQL Server 2000.

IMO we should not have to support TDS 4.2 these days, and in fact pymssql is not supported anyway, @latkinsa can you get clarification on having to use an obsolete TDS version with a much newer SQL server version?

well, not sure why we are running on TDS 4 - it is a part of the standard linux image on our platform, may be nobody bothered to upgrade this since the beginning. I'll raise this question with our ops.

> I wonder why this one column has this issue ? there is a CoerceUnicode datatype in information_schema but it currently doesn't CAST for the actual selected column as that hasn't been a problem. is there something unique about this column?

I've done some experiments and cannot find any meaningful reason.

Using the following query on different sample queries results in
```sql
SELECT name, system_type_name, is_nullable, max_length, collation_name
FROM sys.dm_exec_describe_first_result_set(@query, NULL, 0)
```
|query|name| system_type_name| is_nullable |max_length |collation_name|
|--|--|--|--|--|--|
|`SELECT [INFORMATION_SCHEMA].[COLUMNS].[TABLE_SCHEMA] FROM [INFORMATION_SCHEMA].[COLUMNS]`|TABLE_SCHEMA| nvarchar(128)| 1 |256 |Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_KS_WS_SC|
|`SELECT sys.computed_columns.definition from sys.computed_columns`|definition| nvarchar(max)| 1 |-1 |SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS|
|`SELECT CAST(sys.computed_columns.definition AS TEXT) as cast from sys.computed_columns`|cast| text| 1 |-1 |SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS|

The only meaningful difference is that `definition` is unlimited. 

I've tried changing the fix from `CAST(sys.computed_columns.definition AS  TEXT)` to `CAST(sys.computed_columns.definition AS  NVARCHAR(128))` and it continues to work.
So I guess that tds 4 does not supports `NVARCHAR(max)`

> So I guess that tds 4 does not supports NVARCHAR(max)

Exactly. nvarchar(max) [was introduced in SQL Server 2005](https://stackoverflow.com/a/39790739/2144390).
So should I use text or nvarchar(4000) in this case (Unicode in sqlalchemy) in the fix?
Definitely not [N]TEXT. That's been deprecated since [N]VARCHAR(MAX) became a thing.
